title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous and next pages): for a discrete group G and a normal subgroup M of finite index that is a free Z-module of finite type, Grothendieck pushes the extension 1 -> M -> G -> G/M -> 1 out along M -> V(M) = M (x) G_a. Here V(M) is the vector group scheme over the base S_0, presumably Spec Z. This gives an affine group scheme G_M over S_0, an extension of the finite constant group G/M by V(M). For M' contained in M, the inclusion M' -> M induces V(M') -> V(M) and hence G_{M'} -> G_M, so one gets a projective system. The previous page argues that its limit exists as an affine group scheme, not of finite type.

This page states three things:
(i) Since all finite-index free abelian subgroups of G are commensurable, the pro-object depends only on G. The condition is that G contains a finite-index subgroup which is commutative and of finite type as a Z-module. Grothendieck calls such G "virtabélien": finitely generated virtually abelian, i.e. virtually Z^r (crystallographic-type groups).
(ii) Definition (46): Env(G) = (G_i), a projective system of affine group schemes. Its index set is the normal, commutative, torsion-free (implicitly finite-index) subgroups of G. Env is functorial in G.
(iii) Exactness properties called 'interesting and more or less evident':
- (47) Env(G x G') ≅ Env(G) x_{S_0} Env(G').
- (48)-(49) a short exact sequence 1 -> G'' -> G -> G' -> 1 of virtabelian groups gives a short exact sequence of envelopes; the next page adds 'in a sense that should be made precise'.

The next page treats the typical case G = M = Z, via the sequences 0 -> Z -n-> Z -> Z/n -> 0. G_n is the extension of Z/n by G_a, whose coordinate ring is non-canonically Z[T]^n (choose the set-theoretic section {0,...,n-1}). The transition maps G_{nm} -> G_n are multiplication by m on the G_a-parts.

Modern reading: an integral, unipotent-by-profinite 'algebraic envelope' of a virtually abelian discrete group. Over Q every transition map is an isomorphism on the identity component, so Env(G)_Q is an extension of the profinite completion of G/M by M (x) G_a. This is essentially the Malcev/algebraic hull glued with the profinite completion; for Z it is G_a x Ẑ. Over Z it is genuinely non-trivial:
- The extension class of G_n lies in H^2(Z/n, G_a) = R/nR, which is non-zero over Z.
- The limit of G_a under the multiplication maps has coordinate ring Z ⊕ QT ⊕ QT^2 ⊕ ...
- Functions on Env(Z) restricted to Z are integer quasi-polynomials: on each residue class r mod n they are Z-polynomials in (k-r)/n. This ring contains the integer-valued polynomials binom(k,j); restrict to classes mod j! to see it.

Purpose in the manuscript (the Longue Marche sequel on Galois/Teichmüller theory): apparently to attach group-scheme ('schematic') envelopes over Z to discrete groups such as Z (cusp/inertia-type subgroups) and crystallographic groups. This is a step toward the schematization of discrete groups/homotopy types.
errors: The index set is stated as 'normal subgroups of G that are commutative and torsion-free'; the finite-index condition is implicit and needed. Otherwise e.g. {1} would be an index and the system would not depend only on G in the intended way.

Exactness (49) cannot hold termwise over Z. For instance V(M'') -> V(M) induced by an inclusion of finite index [M:M''] = d is multiplication by d on G_a, which is not a monomorphism over Z (its kernel is non-trivial over F_p for p | d). It holds only after reindexing over cofinal systems (indices M contained in G''), i.e. as an exactness of pro-objects. The next page concedes this ('en un sens qu'il conviendrait de préciser').

Cofinality for (49) also uses that every finite-index subgroup of G'' contains one of the form M ∩ G'', and that images of torsion-free M in G' may have torsion and must be refined. Both are fine for virtually abelian groups (LERF), but this is unstated.
'virtabélien' implicitly requires finite generation; this is included via 'de t.f. en tant que Z-module'.

ideas.what: Notion of 'virtabélien' group: a group containing a finite-index subgroup that is a free abelian group of finite type
ideas.modern_name: finitely generated virtually abelian (virtually Z^r) group; crystallographic-type group
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard notion (Bieberbach-type groups); the term 'virtually' is from Serre-era group theory

ideas.what: Env(G): pro-system of affine group schemes over Z, obtained by pushing out G along M -> M ⊗ G_a for finite-index normal torsion-free abelian M; functorial in G
ideas.modern_name: integral unipotent-by-profinite algebraic hull / relative (pro-algebraic) completion over Z of a virtually abelian group; schematization of discrete groups over Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: Over a field of char 0: Malcev completion, Mostow's algebraic hull, Hain/Deligne relative completion. Integral schematization: Toën ('Le problème de la schématisation de Grothendieck revisité', 2020) and Ekedahl's work on integer-valued polynomials / the Hilbert additive group
ideas.where_published: The general schematization problem appears in Pursuing Stacks and letters (to Breen); this specific Env construction is not known to me in published texts

ideas.what: Multiplicativity Env(G x G') ≅ Env(G) x Env(G') and exactness of Env on short exact sequences (in a pro-sense)
ideas.modern_name: exactness of pro-algebraic / relative completion functors
ideas.usually_credited_to: analogous results for relative completion (Hain) and pro-unipotent completion

missed.claim: Grothendieck's integral envelope Env(Z), the projective limit over n of extensions G_n of Z/n by G_a over Z, has functions that restrict on Z to integer quasi-polynomials. This ring contains the integer-valued polynomials. So Env(Z) maps naturally onto the 'Hilbert additive group' Spec Int(Z), which Toën used (2020) to schematize S^1 over Z. The page thus contains an explicit integral, finite-level model of the schematization of Z/BZ, combining profinite and unipotent pieces, decades before the integral schematization literature.
missed.quote: Ainsi pour G un groupe discret virtabélien, on a construit un pro-schéma, syst. proj. de schémas en groupes affines, en groupes, (que je vais noter (46) Env(G) = (G_i)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral models of homotopy types (Toën, Mandell's E_∞ cochains over Z, Yuan's integral models) are an active topic. Grothendieck's Env offers a concrete pro-finite-type alternative to Spec Int(Z) and could be compared with or used in that theory.

missed.claim: The precise sense in which Env is exact (pro-exactness over Z, fppf/fpqc after passing to the limit) is explicitly left open. Extension beyond virtually abelian groups (e.g. to virtually polycyclic/nilpotent groups, or surface and mapping class groups in the Teichmüller tower) is also not addressed here.
missed.quote: (49) 1 -> Env(G'') -> Env(G) -> Env(G') -> 1 ... en un sens qu'il conviendrait de préciser
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: An integral relative completion with good exactness for virtually polycyclic groups would be useful in anabelian and integral-motivic settings. As far as I know it is not available in this form.

deep.surprise_reason: Defining, over Z, a functorial pro-group-scheme envelope of virtually abelian discrete groups is an unpublished, nontrivial construction tied to Grothendieck's schematization program. Its integral aspect anticipates later integral schematization (Hilbert additive group, Toën), which a specialist might not expect in the Longue Marche sequel. Over Q the construction reduces to known algebraic hulls, and the exactness statements are essentially routine, hence moderate.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads '...ne dépend que de G lui-même — moyennant [or: mais à] la condition qu'il existe...'; the struck word before 'moins' is illegible.
'une pro-schéma' should be 'un pro-schéma'. The inserted correction reads 'syst. proj. de schémas en groupes affines', with something struck after 'groupes'.
The coined term is written 'virtabélien' (underlined, in quotes), presumably short for 'virtuellement abélien'.
In (47) the fibre product is over S_0 (subscript under the ×), not a plain product.
In (48) and (49) the first arrow is '1 →'; in (49) the 'Env' of the first term was rewritten over a struck 'Env'.
The page number at top is '680' (the margin number is '24').
